elements.text: FMSS is a design framework I created in 2023 to bring consistency to user experiences across Facebook ad products.  I championed the vision across multiple Meta organizations, driving adoption across the app and establishing FMSS as a canonical framework for Facebook Design.   Its interaction patterns went on to influence broader industry approaches to ad engagement. In 2025, FMSS generated over $51M in incremental revenue for Meta.
When asked how Facebook app’s navigation works,  a participant in research drew this.

Years of localized optimizations, coupled with product and feature additions, have led to a cluttered Facebook interface with inconsistent, unpredictable navigation.   How might we create more consistent experiences that build trust and enable people to engage with Facebook more confidently?

elements.text: As advertiser demand grew, Facebook expanded to support more ad objectives.   Monetization teams independently implemented their own versions to meet their needs, without considering how the split screen interaction should work across ad experiences. This led to inconsistent navigation and post-click behaviors.   Over time, these differences fragmented users’ ad journey, making it harder for people to know what to expect.

Establish a shared interaction model to create  familiarity and reinforce a consistent user mental  model across ad experiences. 
Build reusable infrastructure to enable system-level updates, reduce maintenance costs, and accelerate  new monetization opportunities.

Ads served a range of objectives, including Onsite and Offsite Conversions, Lead Generation, Business Messages, and App Installs, but shared the same underlying task: moving people from discovery to engagement. 
Inconsistencies persisted as product teams iterated in silos, making cross product changes costly and repetitive.
FMSS Facebook Monetization Split Screen _____  A design framework that establishes  a consistent interaction model across  ad objectives and Facebook surfaces.

I brought the framework to product and design leaders  across Facebook for alignment on its principles, application criteria, and scope.  With leadership support in place, I partnered with Blueprint, Facebook’s Design Systems team, to formalize FMSS in the design library through reusable components, usage guidance, and shared resources. 
This made FMSS accessible to design teams across Meta  and established the foundation for broader adoption.

A framework only creates value when teams can adopt it and drive meaningful results.  Because ad experiences spanned multiple organizations beyond Facebook Monetization (Browser Ecosystem, App & Gaming, Business Messaging, and more), I galvanized teams around a unified vision through design advocacy, strategic reviews, and cross-functional collaboration.  Through a series of cross-org experiments, we validated the framework across existing use cases, demonstrating its ability  to improve user experience and business outcomes.

The unification effort went beyond fixing  a fragmented user experience. It reshaped how video ad post clicks were architected  by establishing a layered system that separated shared infrastructure from experience specific logic.   This scalable foundation enabled faster iteration and system-level improvements, while creating a path for future growth.   With the system in place, we brought  ad split screen experiences to Facebook  on iPad for the first time.
